Adaptive Sampling (Sparse Grid) is a rendering optimization that exploits coherence in projections—often introduced by sensing device blurring—to reduce computational overhead by casting a sparse grid of rays (less than one per pixel) and adaptively increasing ray density in regions of high image complexity [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that an optimization takes advantage of coherence in projections (often from sensing device blurring) by casting a sparse grid of rays (less than one per pixel) and adaptively increasing the number of rays in regions of high image complexity. It also mentions forming images via interpolation and resampling, and notes the risk of missing small polygons when integrating with adaptive supersampling if the initial sampling rate is too low. All specific details in the claim are present in the provided text.
